OUR APPROACH

title: People on the UP3DCYCLING
text:
UP3DCYCLING is coordinated by Associate Professor (Maître de conférences)  Fabio A. Cruz Sanchez. He works at the École Nationale Supérieure en Génie des Systèmes et de l’Innovation (ENSGSI) and a researcher at the ERPI Laboratory (Équipe de Recherche sur les Processus Innovatifs), Université de Lorraine, Nancy, France. His research focuses on distributed recycling through additive manufacturing (DRAM), open-source manufacturing technologies and the development of sustainable production systems based on circular economy principles. His main research interests include plastic and polymer recycling, 3D printing and additive manufacturing, open-source hardware, distributed manufacturing networks, and the technical, logistical and environmental assessment of recycling processes. He also investigates the role of FabLabs and collaborative innovation spaces in enabling local recycling initiatives, closing material loops and promoting socio-technical transitions towards more sustainable and decentralized manufacturing systems.









Mauricio Camargo is a Professor of Technology and Innovation Management at the École Nationale Supérieure en Génie des Systèmes et de l’Innovation (ENSGSI), Université de Lorraine, in Nancy, France, and Director of the ERPI Laboratory (Research Team on Innovative Processes). His research focuses on innovation engineering and the management, design and evaluation of innovation processes. His main research interests include new product development, decision-making in product and process design, technology and innovation management, and multi-criteria and multi-objective decision-support methods. He also investigates collaborative and interdisciplinary approaches to innovation, including Open Innovation and Living Labs, as well as the development of methodologies and tools to support innovation strategies and the sustainable transformation of industrial and organizational systems









Hakim Boudaoud is a Professor at the École Nationale Supérieure en Génie des Systèmes et de l’Innovation (ENSGSI) and a researcher at the ERPI Laboratory (Équipe de Recherche sur les Processus Innovatifs) at Université de Lorraine, Nancy, France. His research focuses on mechanical engineering, additive manufacturing and the development of innovative and sustainable materials and production processes. His main research interests include polymer recycling and circular economy, open-source and distributed additive manufacturing, mechanical characterization and modelling of materials, and the optimization of 3D-printing processes. He also investigates the potential of open-source hardware and decentralized manufacturing technologies to support local recycling initiatives, reduce environmental impacts and promote more sustainable production systems.









Laurent Dupont is a Research Engineer (HDR – Accreditation to Supervise Research) at the Université de Lorraine and a researcher at the ERPI Laboratory (Équipe de Recherche sur les Processus Innovatifs). His research focuses on innovation engineering, collaborative design and user-driven innovation, particularly in the context of smart and sustainable cities and territories. His main research interests include Living Labs and Fab Living Labs, open innovation spaces, collaborative innovation processes, user participation in the design and evaluation of new products and services, and immersive collaborative environments. He is also interested in the role of digital technologies, data-driven approaches and multi-stakeholder partnerships in supporting urban transformation and sustainable territorial development. He is co-founder and scientific manager of the Lorraine Fab Living Lab and co-creator of the Lorraine Smart Cities Living Lab, where he develops and experiments with methodologies for collaborative innovation involving citizens, businesses, researchers and public authorities.

section: Laboratoire Réactions et Génie des Procédés – Université de Lorraine
text:
Laboratoire Réactions et Génie des Procédés – Université de Lorraine











Cécile Nouvel is a Professor at the École Nationale Supérieure des Industries Chimiques (ENSIC) and a researcher at the Laboratoire Réactions et Génie des Procédés (LRGP). Her research focuses on polymer product engineering, particularly the design, formulation, processing and characterization of functional polymeric materials. Her main research interests include the synthesis and development of functional (co)polymers, polymer emulsifiers and nanoemulsions, polymer processing by extrusion and 3D printing, and the development of advanced materials for biomedical applications and drug delivery. More recently, her research also addresses sustainable polymer materials, including recycling and innovative processing strategies to improve material performance and recyclability.









Sandrine Hoppe is a CNRS researcher at the Laboratoire Réactions et Génie des Procédés (LRGP) in Nancy, France. Her research focuses on the development, processing and characterization of polymeric materials with controlled properties and structures. Her main research interests include polymer processing and reactive extrusion, micro- and nanostructured polymer composites, bio-based and sustainable materials, and the valorization and recycling of plastics. She also works on process modelling, simulation and optimization, with the aim of developing innovative and more sustainable materials and manufacturing processes

section: Free Appropriate Sustainable Technology (FAST) – Western University
text:
Free Appropriate Sustainable Technology (FAST) – Western University











Joshua Pearce is the director of the Free Appropriate Sustainability Technology research group – https://www.appropedia.org/FAST at the Western University, which is recognized as one of world’s top 20 universities in new global sustainability rankings top 20 ranked universities for sustainability. Prof. Joshua Pearce’ research is on the use of open source appropriate technology (OSAT) to find collaborative solutions to problems in sustainability and to reduce poverty. His research spans areas of engineering of solar photovoltaic technology, open hardware, and distributed recycling and additive manufacturing (DRAM) using RepRap 3-D printing, but also includes policy and economics.









Alessia Romani is a Western Postdoctoral Fellowship Awardee and Postdoctoral Associate at FAST Lab, Western University (Canada). Her work lies at the intersection of product and engineering design, materials, digital fabrication, and sustainability, with a focus on circular practices and open design. Her research experience and background merge materials engineering with product and engineering design, developing and characterising sustainable materials for design and 3D printing, and keeping a hands-on and application-driven approach.

title: People on the UP3DCYCLING
text:
Laboratoire Interdisciplinaire Sciences Innovations Sociétés











Baptiste Monsaingeon is a sociologist specializing in science, technology, and the environment. A lecturer at the University of Reims Champagne-Ardenne, he is currently on secondment as a research fellow at the CNRS, within the LISIS. His research focuses on analyzing the relationships between contemporary societies and their waste. Since 2016, he has been particularly interested in plastics, seeking to reconstruct their socio-technical trajectories—both in terms of the history of their production and uses, as well as their impacts and regulation. Between 2022 and 2025, he served as scientific co-leader in charge of the social and human sciences (SHS) for the INRAE and CNRS Collective Scientific Expertise on plastics used in agriculture and food (ESCo Plastiques). In 2024, he received the CNRS Bronze Medal.

Give a new purpose to post-consumer plastics.





OUR APPRAOCH

Multi-level perspective of the Distributed Upcycling
Our overall research aims is to study, implement, and evaluate the upcycling potential of mixed plastic waste via in-situ reactive compatibilization using open-source additive manufacturing.
UP3DCYCLING project is supported by multidisciplinary expertise spanning three domains: 1) polymer science, 2) additive manufacturing processes, and 3) socio-technical systems. The interaction across these three levels is supported by experimental, modeling, and scenario approaches, which constitute a key added value of the project, enabling a holistic understanding of both technical and social dynamics.

title: Ethnographic Analysis of Urban Manufacturing Ecosystems
text:
Objective of the Internship
The internship takes place at an exploratory stage of the project, ahead of the in-depth ethnographic fieldwork in Nancy that will be carried out as part of a PhD (starting end of 2027). Its main goals are:

To map the actors, networks and public action frameworks shaping citizen-led plastic upcycling in urban manufacturing settings, from the Nancy area (local waste governance, metropolitan authority, waste collection, reuse and repair organizations, public support for third places) to regional and national networks.
To build an analytical framework and a first set of contrasts that will help situate the Nancy case (Green Fablab, Octroi Nancy third place) in the subsequent fieldwork.

title: Ethnographic Analysis of Urban Manufacturing Ecosystems
text:
Deliverable

A mapping report of the actors, networks and public action frameworks relevant to distributed plastic upcycling, from the Nancy area to the national level.
A scientific document presenting the analytical framework, the methodology and the first results, as a basis for the PhD fieldwork.
Participation on a scientific/practitioner conference is intended. Networks collaboration will be established during the internship.
